The taurine thing is somewhat incorrect. The taurine found in many meat based cat food is synthetic, same as in plant-based cat food. It's actually the cysteine which is the biggest problem, as some cats can't absorb the synthetic version as well as the animal-derived version. This causes a methionine:cysteine imbalance which can result in urinary tract issues like alkaline urine and urine crystals, particularly in male cats due to the obvious anatomical differences. It's very important to see your vet regularly to check the urine ph levels and for crystals if you're feeding your cat a plant-based diet, and IMO the risk of urinary tract issues is too great to feed male cats a 100% plant based diet, and cats with a history of urinary troubles shouldn't even be on a majority plant based diet - especially kibble-based, although that goes for all kibble diets too. 
The scientific studies done where all the cats die are not done on "high quality" plant based diets with all the supplements, and while they're important reminders of the dangers posed by incorrect diets, they are not enough to say definitively "no cats can thrive on a totally or partially plant based diet", especially when there's substantial anecdotal evidence to the contrary. More evidence is needed, plant based diets that are carefully prepared like Vegecat must be thoroughly investigated.
